rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation at real reply structures (with an amendment before the real run), 32 replication periods (43 units), three natives (G12, G26, G23), scorecard, 190 estimates rows, confirmatory script frozen and dry-run. Holdout not run; two natives underpowered. Round 1c: validated v2.1 disagreement flag, label-noise null (synthetic-validated), per-agent verdict read timing, 138 estimates rows.
rationale.faithfulness: The settlement switch-off in #12 beats team permutation, two-way agent effects, a heat field and remanence, with soft and hard labels. The competition contrast beats the prize-free set but rests on an unvalidated stance subtype in four regime-I periods, and no rival-specific antagonism appears outside #12. Scorecard all 1s except I. 1c: the #12 switch-off is sharper with the validated flag (0 of 64 post-verdict opponent replies flagged); the competition contrast is killed, so the verdict narrows.
rationale.usefulness: A monitor-level rule: stance antagonism tracks the incentive state, so settling a prize ends it within minutes and rival roles without a single winner do not create feuds. Effects are small outside assigned debates.

one_line: Settling a prize switches assigned antagonism off by the first reply after the verdict is read; competition without sides adds no validated disagreement.
